paper_metadata.title: A performance characterization of quantum generative models

experiments.description: Quantum circuit Born machine (QCBM) benchmark on synthetic and real low-dimensional data using a continuous circuit architecture and min-max or PIT preprocessing.

algorithm.ansatz: data re-uploading variational circuit with RX(z), RZ(theta), RY(theta), RZ(theta) blocks and CNOT entanglers
algorithm.convergence_criteria: maximum allowed epochs or when KL divergence change between successive steps drops below a threshold

hyperparameters.shots_for_expectation: exact expectation values computed with state-vector simulator; no shot sampling used in simulation

algorithm.parameter_initialization: subsequent blocks initialized from previously fitted parameters; new block parameters initialized to zero / identity

problem_formulation.encoding_details: one qubit per data dimension; random noise z inserted via single-qubit rotations
problem_formulation.objective_function: minimize Kullback-Leibler divergence CKL(Q, P(theta)) between training-data histogram Q and generated-sample histogram P(theta)

problem_instance.description: Learn low-dimensional probability distributions from synthetic and real financial data.

speedup_claims.conditions: 3D X data set: classical GAN with 9475 parameters vs QGAN discrete copula with 54 parameters
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a parameter-efficiency claim, not a runtime speedup; based on one highlighted case in the text.

experiments.description: Quantum circuit Born machine (QCBM) benchmark on synthetic and real low-dimensional data using a discrete standard circuit architecture and min-max preprocessing.

algorithm.ansatz: discrete standard variational circuit with RY and RYY gates
algorithm.convergence_criteria: maximum allowed epochs or when KL divergence change between successive steps drops below a threshold
algorithm.parameter_initialization: subsequent blocks initialized from previously fitted parameters; new block parameters initialized to zero / identity

problem_formulation.encoding_details: discretize each dimension with 4 qubits; 8 qubits for 2D and 12 qubits for 3D
problem_formulation.objective_function: minimize Kullback-Leibler divergence CKL(Q, P(theta)) between training-data histogram Q and generated-sample histogram P(theta)

problem_instance.description: Learn low-dimensional probability distributions from synthetic and real financial data.

speedup_claims.conditions: 3D X data set: classical GAN with 9475 parameters vs QCBM discrete copula with 60? (text/table indicates 54-162 range; highlighted case uses 54 parameters for QGAN, 162 for QCBM in 3D X)
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper’s explicit two-orders-of-magnitude claim is for quantum models generally versus classical on O/X data; this row is a parameter-efficiency comparison, not runtime.

experiments.description: Quantum circuit Born machine (QCBM) benchmark on synthetic and real low-dimensional data using a discrete copula circuit architecture and PIT preprocessing.

algorithm.ansatz: copula variational circuit with initial Hadamard and CNOT entanglement followed by RZ-RX-RZ / RX-RZ-RX style single-qubit rotations and RXX entanglers
algorithm.convergence_criteria: maximum allowed epochs or when KL divergence change between successive steps drops below a threshold
algorithm.parameter_initialization: subsequent blocks initialized from previously fitted parameters; new block parameters initialized to zero / identity

problem_formulation.encoding_details: PIT-transformed data learned as a copula on a discrete grid; 8 qubits for 2D and 12 qubits for 3D
problem_formulation.objective_function: minimize Kullback-Leibler divergence CKL(Q, P(theta)) between training-data histogram Q and generated-sample histogram P(theta)
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: copula structure enforced by initial maximally entangled state and no inter-register entangling gates after initialization

problem_instance.description: Learn low-dimensional probability distributions from synthetic and real financial data.

speedup_claims.conditions: 3D X data set: classical GAN with 9475 parameters vs discrete copula QGAN with 54 parameters
speedup_claims.caveats: Parameter-efficiency claim only; not a runtime benchmark.

experiments.description: Quantum generative adversarial network (QGAN) benchmark with a continuous quantum generator and classical discriminator on synthetic and real low-dimensional data.

algorithm.variant: QGAN with continuous quantum generator and classical neural-network discriminator
algorithm.ansatz: data re-uploading variational circuit with RX(z), RZ(theta), RY(theta), RZ(theta) blocks and CNOT entanglers
algorithm.convergence_criteria: trained for a set number of epochs; performance tracked by KL divergence

problem_formulation.encoding_details: one qubit per data dimension; random noise z inserted via single-qubit rotations
problem_formulation.objective_function: GAN min-max objective with discriminator loss LD and generator loss LG; evaluated via KL divergence after training

problem_instance.description: Learn low-dimensional probability distributions from synthetic and real financial data.

experiments.description: Quantum generative adversarial network (QGAN) benchmark with a discrete quantum generator and classical discriminator on synthetic and real low-dimensional data.

algorithm.variant: QGAN with discrete standard or discrete copula quantum generator and classical neural-network discriminator
algorithm.ansatz: discrete standard circuit with RY/RYY gates or discrete copula circuit with initial Hadamard/CNOT entanglement and RZ-RX-RZ / RX-RZ-RX plus RXX gates
algorithm.convergence_criteria: trained for a set number of epochs; performance tracked by KL divergence

problem_formulation.encoding_details: discretize each dimension with 4 qubits; 8 qubits for 2D and 12 qubits for 3D; one shot per sample
problem_formulation.objective_function: GAN min-max objective with discriminator loss LD and generator loss LG; evaluated via KL divergence after training
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: for copula variant, initial maximally entangled state and no inter-register entangling gates after initialization
